items.front: Statutory vs constitutional vs executive — the test?
items.back: Statutory = created by an Act (NHRC, CVC, SEBI, NGT, Lokpal, CIC); Constitutional = named in the Constitution (ECI, CAG, UPSC); Executive = by resolution (NITI Aayog, Law Commission).
items.examPoint: Constitutional vs statutory vs executive — classification

items.front: NHRC — statute, 2019 change, and armed-forces limit?
items.back: Protection of Human Rights Act 1993; 2019 amendment lets a former SC judge (not only ex-CJI) chair and cut term 5→3 yrs; recommendatory; cannot directly investigate the armed forces.

items.front: CBI — legal basis and the State-consent rule?
items.back: Delhi Special Police Establishment (DSPE) Act 1946 (SPE 1941 → CBI 1963 resolution); under Ministry of Personnel; needs a State's general consent (Sec 6 DSPE) to operate there.

items.front: CVC — origin, statute, power over CBI?
items.back: Set up 1964 (Santhanam Committee); statutory since CVC Act 2003; Central Vigilance Commissioner + 2 VCs; can direct and supervise the CBI in corruption cases; advisory.

items.front: Lokpal — statute, composition, jurisdiction over PM?
items.back: Lokpal & Lokayuktas Act 2013; Chairperson + up to 8 members (≥half judicial); covers the PM with safeguards (excludes intl relations, security, atomic energy, space). 1st Chair: Justice P.C. Ghose.

items.front: CIC — statute, size, and the 2019 change?
items.back: RTI Act 2005; Chief Information Commissioner + up to 10 ICs; appointed by President on a committee (PM, LoP, a Union Minister). RTI (Amendment) 2019 let the Centre fix tenure/salaries.

items.front: Regulator statute-years: RBI, SEBI, TRAI, IRDAI, CCI, PFRDA?
items.back: RBI 1934, SEBI Act 1992 (body 1988), TRAI 1997, IRDAI 1999, CCI (Competition Act 2002, operational 2009), PFRDA 2013. All statutory; combine rule-making + supervision + quasi-judicial penalties.
NGT Act 2010; quasi-judicial; judicial + expert (scientific) members; orders binding, can award compensation; appeals lie to the Supreme Court.

items.front: Tribunals in the Constitution — which amendment, which articles?
items.back: 42nd Amendment 1976 added Art 323A (administrative tribunals, e.g. CAT for service matters) and Art 323B (taxation, environment, etc.).
The 99th Amendment (2014) set up the NJAC; the Supreme Court struck it down (2015) as violating judicial independence, restoring the collegium system.
items.examPoint: 99th Amendment / NJAC struck down; collegium restored

items.front: NALSA & Gram Nyayalayas — statutes and key facts?
items.back: NALSA — Legal Services Authorities Act 1987 (patron CJI; Lok Adalats; free legal aid). Gram Nyayalayas — Act 2008; try BOTH civil and criminal cases; allow social activists as mediators.
items.examPoint: NALSA & Legal Services Authorities Act 1987 (Lok Adalats)

items.front: Tea Board & Forest Rights Act — the exam traps?
items.back: Tea Board: statutory, under Ministry of Commerce (NOT Agriculture), HQ Kolkata (NOT Bengaluru). FRA 2006 nodal ministry = Ministry of Tribal Affairs (Gram Sabha initiates claims).
items.examPoint: Commodity Boards — Tea Board (Ministry of Commerce, HQ Kolkata)

items.front: NDMA, Law Commission, UGC — nature and heads?
items.back: NDMA — Disaster Management Act 2005, PM is ex-officio Chairperson (State: CM). Law Commission — non-statutory (1955 resolution), advice not binding. UGC — UGC Act 1956, regulates higher education.
items.examPoint: NDMA, Law Commission, UGC — basis & headship
items.source: APPSC GK; DM Act 2005; UGC Act 1956
